p: these things Paul departed from Athens: The true ministers are so far from seeking their own profit, that they willingly depart from what is rightfully theirs, rather than hindering the course of the Gospel in the slightest way.
Claudius had commanded all Jews to: Suetonius records that Rome banished the Jews because they were never at rest, and that because of Christ.
And he reasoned in the synagogue: The truth ought always to be freely uttered, yet nonetheless the doctrine may be moderated in accordance with the hearers, so that they are most profited.
persuaded the Jews and the Greeks: Exhorted so that he persuaded, and that is what the word signifies.

was pressed in the spirit: Was very much grieved in mind: by which is signified the great earnestness of his mind, which was greatly moved: for Paul was so zealous that he completely forgot himself, and with a wonderful courage gave himself to preach Christ.
And when they opposed themselves: Although we have tried all possible means, and yet in vain, we must not stop our work, but forsake the rebellious, and go to those that are more obedient.

blood be upon your own heads: This is a type of speech taken from the Hebrews, by which he means that the Jews are the cause of their own destruction, and as for him, that he is without fault in forsaking them and going to other nations.
Then spake the Lord to Paul: God does confirm and maintain the steadfastness of his servants.

continued there a year and six: Literally, "sat", whereupon they in former time took the name of their bishop's seat: but Paul sat, that is, continued teaching the word of God: and this type of seat does not belong to those who never took their seats with a mind to teach in them.
And when Gallio was the deputy: The wicked are never weary of doing evil, but the Lord wonderfully mocks their endeavours.

Achaia: That is, of Greece, yet the Romans did not call him deputy of Greece, but of Achaia, because the Romans brought the Greeks into subjection by the Achaians, who in those days were Princes of Greece, as Pausanias records.
reason would that I should bear: As much as I rightly could.
words and: As if a man has not spoken well, as judged by your religion.
names: For this profane man thinks that the controversy of religion is merely a fight about words, and over nothing important.
And Paul after this tarried there: Paul is made all to all, to win all to Christ.
having shorn his head in: That is, Paul.
Cenchrea: Cenchrea was a haven of the Corinthians.
When they desired him to tarry: The apostles were carried about not by the will of man, but by the leading of the Holy Spirit.
if God will: So we should promise nothing without this clause, for we do not know what the following day will bring forth.

And a certain Jew named Apollos: Apollos, a godly and learned man, does not refuse to profit in the school of a base and abject handicraftsman, and also of a woman: and so becomes and excellent minister of the Church.
mighty in the scriptures: Very well instructed in the knowledge of the scriptures.
way of God more perfectly: The way that leads to God.
grace: Through God's gracious favour, or by those excellent gifts which God had bestowed upon him.
